newsitem.title: UK: UK Asians back Labour despite economic confidence.
newsitem.headline: UK Asians back Labour despite economic confidence.

text.p: British voters of south Asian origin are confident about the state of the economy but their vote will overwhelmingly go to the opposition Labour Party in the coming election, a MORI poll published on Tuesday found.
MORI interviewed 1,003 south Asian people by telephone between January 31 and February 9.
Seventy percent said they were likely to vote Labour, up from 64 percent that did so in the 1992 election, while the Conservative vote is likely to drop to 25 from 31 percent.
Worries about the economy are not to blame for the fall in Conservative support, judging by the findings.
Thirty percent of respondents said they felt the economy would stay the same over the next year and 32 percent forecast an improvement, against 24 percent who saw a deterioration.
Labour leader Tony Blair's standing was high. Sixty percent were satisfied with his performance, against only 35 percent who were happy with Prime Minister John Major.
Asked which party they trusted most to look after the interests of Asian people in Britain, 51 percent replied Labour and just 15 percent Conservative.
The survey was commissioned by Zee TV, the world's largest Asian television network. It claims half a million viewers in Britain, or one in three Asian households.

Zee TV said the south Asian vote in Britain -- voters with Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi roots -- was clustered in particular areas, enhancing its importance in the coming election, due to be held by end-May.
"There are 45 seats in which the Asian population outweighs the 1992 margin of victory for the winning party and an unprecedented 36 Asian candidates are standing for the coming elections," it said.
